name: Safari
statusNote: Actively developed as Apple's platform browser.

windows.note: Apple no longer distributes current Safari for Windows.

ios.note: Included with iOS; all iOS browsers use WebKit under Apple's platform rules.

availability.cpuNotes: Current releases follow supported Apple hardware and OS versions.

foundation.codeLicense: WebKit open source with Apple proprietary browser and platform integration

telemetry.note: Apple documents privacy-preserving product analytics and settings separately from website protection.

trackerBlocking.note: Intelligent Tracking Prevention limits cross-site tracking.

fingerprintingProtections.note: Safari documents fingerprinting defenses such as reducing identifying configuration detail.

privacy.privateWindows: Private Browsing limits local history and adds privacy protections; it is not anonymity.

vpnOrProxy.note: No general VPN is included in Safari itself.

manifestV2.note: Safari does not use Chrome's extension distribution contract.

manifestV3.note: Safari Web Extensions support selected Chromium-compatible APIs with platform differences.

extensions.limitations: Safari extensions are distributed through the App Store and have WebKit-specific API and entitlement constraints.

nativeContentBlocking.note: Safari supports native content-blocking rule lists and tracking prevention.

verticalTabs.note: The sidebar lists tab groups vertically, but the tab strip itself has no vertical layout mode.

workspaces.note: Tab Groups provide a workspace-like grouping model.

profiles.note: Profiles or equivalent browser identities are available.

splitView.note: macOS Safari has no in-window page tiling; iPad Split View is an OS windowing feature, not a Safari tab tile.

sidebar.note: The sidebar provides tab groups, bookmarks, and reading list.

sync.note: iCloud sync covers supported Safari data.

translation.note: Safari offers translation for supported pages and languages.

pwa.note: Progressive web apps are supported by the Chromium install flow.

iosEngine.note: Safari is Apple's own browser and is not subject to the third-party engine rule; it is WebKit by definition.

assistant.note: Apple Intelligence provides a built-in assistant surface.

summarization.note: Apple Intelligence documents page or multi-tab summarisation.

agenticActions.note: Apple Intelligence documents multi-step actions taken on the user's behalf.

aiSearch.note: An AI answer engine is not documented.

contentGeneration.note: Apple Intelligence documents text or image generation.

aiPrivacyControls.note: Apple Intelligence documents retention, training or kill-switch controls.

crossTabContext.note: Apple Intelligence documents awareness of multiple tabs or history.

voiceMultimodal.note: Apple Intelligence documents voice or image interaction.

dataSaver.note: No documented data-saving or compression mode.

mobileExtensions.note: Safari extensions install on iOS and are managed in Settings.

setAsDefault.note: Safari is the platform default; the setting lives in iOS rather than in the browser.

desktopSiteMode.note: Request Desktop Website is documented in the iPhone user guide.

downloadManager.note: A downloads location setting is documented; no separate manager screen is named.

offlineReading.note: Reading List items can be saved automatically for offline reading.

biometricLock.note: Private Browsing can require Face ID, Touch ID, or the passcode to unlock.

backgroundMedia.note: Background or picture-in-picture playback is not documented.

webPush.note: Web push support is not documented.
